Apache Arrow · Rust 1.95 · WebAssembly components

Batch pipelines that
work out their own order

Write transforms in Rust. Say which columns each one reads and writes. PCS derives the execution plan, runs independent work concurrently, and ships the whole pipeline as a WebAssembly component.

Build your first pipeline Read the concepts

The idea in one diagram

You never write a stage list. Each system declares the fields it touches, and that declaration is enough for PCS to work out what can run together.

Why columns

Storing each field as a contiguous Arrow column, rather than a row per record, changes what the machine has to move.

▮

Read only what you touch

A system reading 3 of 50 columns loads 24 MB instead of 400 MB per million rows. The rest never enters cache.

⇄

Handoff is a pointer

Passing a batch between stages is an Arc clone — one atomic increment, no buffer copy.

◇

Checkpoints are a memcpy

Arrow IPC writes contiguous buffers, so crash recovery decodes 19× faster than a row-oriented equivalent at 1M rows.

See the benchmark numbers and how they were measured

Is PCS a fit?

Reach for PCS when
  • Batches are 100k–100M rows and latency is measured in seconds, not microseconds
  • The transform is imperative Rust that SQL expresses awkwardly
  • Schemas are wide — tens to hundreds of columns, of which each step reads a few
  • You need recovery time to be a design constraint, not an afterthought
Look elsewhere when
  • You want SQL — there is no query planner here; DataFusion will win
  • You need sub-millisecond streaming — PCS is batch-first by design
  • You are building a game engine — the ECS vocabulary is a naming nod, nothing more
  • Your data is under ~10k rows — a plain Vec will beat this

Five concepts, in order

Each one builds on the previous. Read them in this order and nothing will be forward-referenced.

01

Dataset

The columnar container. One Arrow RecordBatch per registered Component, all sharing a row count.
02

System

One transform, plus the meta() that names which columns it reads and writes.
03

Pipeline

A Dataset and its Systems. Turns declarations into stages, and retries what fails.
04

Scheduler

Several independent Pipelines in one process, with dependency edges between them.
05

Distributed Runner

The same Pipeline against claimed row ranges across nodes, checkpointed through Raft.

How a pipeline ships

PCS is service-first. You do not deploy a binary containing your pipeline; you deploy pcs-service once and hand it components.

Where this project is

PCS is a playground for two questions: how far specialised coding agents can maintain a non-trivial multi-crate Rust codebase, and what a Rust-native batch engine with WebAssembly extensibility should look like. It is not production-ready, and the crates are not published to crates.io. Feedback and contributions are welcome.
